description: A ground-level photograph depicting extensive coastal salines (salt pans) under a clear blue sky. The foreground shows dry, brown earth with sparse vegetation. The middle ground is dominated by numerous rectangular and polygonal evaporation ponds, clearly separated by earthen embankments. These ponds exhibit a variety of colours, ranging from bright white (indicating crystallised salt) to light pink, pale blue-green, and deeper blue, reflecting different stages of brine concentration or salt production. To the left, a larger body of water is visible, possibly a lagoon or sea inlet. In the background, distant, arid-looking hills or mountains rise above the horizon. This image illustrates land use typical of the CORINE Land Cover (CLC) class 422 Salines, which are exploited for salt production by evaporation, often involving parcellation and embankment systems.
